The front door of Kate's apartment opens onto a cramped entrance hall. Several pairs of shoes have been kicked off and left where they fell — low-top skaters, strappy heels, a single boot with no partner in sight. A set of keys hangs from a hook that's half-pulled from the wall, and a faded welcome mat has had something rude embroidered over the original message in bright pink thread.

The air smells faintly of her perfume — something sweet and heavy that clings to everything in this place.

A narrow hallway connects the rooms of Kate's apartment. The walls are lined with framed photographs of people you don't recognise — other demons, mostly, caught mid-laugh or mid-drink at parties that look like they happened decades ago. A coat stand by the wall is holding considerably more lingerie than coats.

The carpet is worn but clean enough, and faint music drifts from somewhere deeper in the apartment — something low and slow.

Kate's kitchen is a tiny, utilitarian space that's seen better days. Takeaway boxes are stacked in a precarious tower beside the bin, and the countertop is mostly occupied by an extremely expensive-looking coffee machine that's clearly the most valued object in the room. A single mug sits beside it bearing a slogan that would make most people blush.

There's one clean plate in the drying rack. Just one.

The lounge is a study in comfortable neglect. A worn velvet sofa — deep plum, sagging in the middle — faces a flat-screen that's been left on and muted, flickering through some daytime programme. Fashion magazines are stacked on every available surface, interspersed with empty glasses and the occasional stray piece of jewellery.

A blanket lies crumpled on the sofa, still holding the impression of someone who fell asleep here recently and didn't bother to tidy up. The curtains are half-drawn, letting in slats of dusty light.

Kate's bedroom is dominated by a large, unmade bed with rumpled black sheets and too many pillows. Blackout curtains are drawn against the daylight, leaving the room in a dim, warm half-dark. Clothes are scattered across the floor — a skater dress draped over a chair, underwear in a trail toward the bathroom.

The air in here is heavier — her perfume, yes, but something warmer underneath it. Lived-in. Intimate. A vanity table against one wall is cluttered with cosmetics, and a full-length mirror beside it has a crack running diagonally across the glass.

#IF(game.getDialogueFlags().getSavedLong("kate_dogmeat_offscreen_count") >= 9)

A large dog bed sits at the foot of the bed, a folded blanket laid neatly inside it. #IF(game.getDialogueFlags().getSavedLong("kate_dogmeat_offscreen_count") >= 16) 'Dogmeat' has been stitched into the blanket in the same bright pink thread as the welcome mat downstairs. #ENDIF It's the tidiest thing in the room.

#ENDIF

Every surface in Kate's bathroom is covered in cosmetics and hair products — bottles, tubes, and jars crowding each other for space on the sink, the windowsill, and even the edge of the claw-foot tub in the corner. Half-melted candles have been lit so many times they're just lumps of coloured wax fused to whatever surface they were last set down on.

The mirror above the sink has a lipstick mark on it — a perfect kiss print in dark red. A fluffy towel is draped over the tub's edge, and the whole room smells of expensive shampoo and steam.
